contentText:
Troye Sivan reveals how Madonna cleared the sample on “Party,” and why that moment became a major creative unlock for the song. He walks us through the writing process, and how the track evolved from early versions into the final club-ready record. Sivan also opens up about the emotional whiplash of his new era, releasing “She’s the Best” and then pivoting into the rush of “Party.” He reveals what he actually measures success by, the cultural conversation he hopes the music and videos spark, and the way he balances bold pop moments with more interior, vulnerable storytelling. Plus, Troye shares what it was like working with Nicole Kidman, breaks down “Cowboy,” “Canada Dry,” “Sex Star,” “Troye Meets World,” “FF” and more!

Troye Sivan 

It’s like my favorite moment in the video, like as I’m kind of diving in. Hi, I’m Troye Sivan and this is Billboard News.

Tetris Kelly 

Party in the bush, party in the Billboard office with Troye Sivan.

Ooh.

How you doing?

Good. How are you?

I’m so happy you’re here, man. We got so much to talk about, so let’s jump right into it.

Cool.

So you dropped “She’s the Best,” immediately followed by “Party.” What has it been like to see the reaction so far online to your new music?

It’s been crazy. I think I, um, I’ve been honestly kind of like pleasantly surprised because I definitely have been like pushing myself I think, and maybe in turn also like pushing people, and I wasn’t really sure how. . . I, you know, I, I know that kind of like when the album arrives, I think everything kind of becomes like clearer and kind of clicks into place. But the sort of journey that I wanted to take people on to get there is definitely like a bit of a rollercoaster. And so going from something like as sensitive as “She’s The Best” into something as like kind of irreverent as “Party,” I, I’ve been very excited [laughs] to kind of like do that, and it’s been, it’s been fun and I’ve been, I’ve been really happy with how it’s all kind of like being received.
